newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency denies planning to axe nuclear unit.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency denies planning to axe nuclear unit.

text.p: Japan's Science and Technology Agency, which supervises nuclear technology, on Friday denied a report that it had decided to scrap the troubled Tokaimura nuclear reprocessing plant north of Tokyo.

"It's a total lie," said a senior official at the agency, referring to a domestic media report that said the government had decided to permanently shut the plant, which has a capacity to reprocess 90 tonnes of used nuclear fuel a year.
The fate of the facility has been a central theme in the ongoing debate over Japan's nuclear policy since a fire and explosion at the plant exposed 37 workers to low-level radiation in March.
The plant has been closed since the accidents.
"The reprocessing plant is integral to the development of fast-breeder nuclear reactor technology," the official said.
"From that point of view, it is unthinkable that we would scrap the plant."
The reprocessing facility is scheduled to undergo major maintenance checks from November and is likely to remain shut until then, the official said.
He also said the maintenance work is needed because the agency intends to operate the plant again.
